title: Canary Timeline Collage — lightweight scenario templates and micro-briefs for non-engineer operators
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Operators outside SRE/Platform (PMs, product owners, support leads) find the existing canary composer too technical — they want a single-screen story that communicates risk, expected impact, and an easy rollback checklist. Goal: Create a lightweight "timeline collage" pattern: a compact, visually-scannable canary timeline that presents scenario templates (e.g., feature flag ramp, A/B test, config toggle), short micro-briefs for each template (what to watch, success indicators), and an emergency rollback card with one-tap actions. Scope: design screens for Composer canvas, one Template picker, one Timeline summary card, Emergency Rollback card with required confirmations. Out of scope: backend gating logic, quota enforcement UI, RBAC policy changes.
acceptance_criteria: Template library accessible from Composer with 5 prebuilt templates: gradual-ramp, 50-50 A/B, targeted-segment, shadow-traffic, config-toggle
Timeline collage shows per-template micro-briefs (1 sentence) and 3 auto-calculated observability signals
Emergency Rollback card exposes 1-click rollback, a minimal confirmation modal, and an audit annotation field
Design annotated Figma frames (desktop) delivered with copy and ARIA hints for accessibility
Validated with at least 4 non-engineer participants in a moderated usability session and addressed top 3 friction points
comments: 2025-02-14 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff — outlined problem and scope with PM and Eng. Agreed to focus on non-engineer persona for initial prototype.
2025-02-17 - Marco Li: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma. Shared three layout variants: stacked timeline, card collage, and mini-map lane. Feedback: PM prefers card collage for scannability.
2025-02-19 - Ravi Shah (PM): Suggested adding automatic signal suggestions (latency, error rate, cost delta) to the micro-brief; engineering to validate feasibility (ENG-72000).

2025-02-21 - Marco Li: Iteration 2 — added Emergency Rollback card, one-tap rollback flow sketch, and compact confirmation microcopy. Raised concern about accidental rollbacks; proposed two-step annotation confirmation instead of password.

2025-02-24 - Usability session (4 participants - PMs and Support leads): Observations — participants liked single-line brief and success indicators, but wanted clearer signposting of who can execute rollback and where it runs (region/capacity).
2025-02-25 - Aisha Patel: Addressed usability feedback — added small 'Invoker role' pill and 'Rollback scope' summary. Updated figma.
2025-02-27 - Elena Gomez (Design lead): Reviewed and requested accessibility hints for keyboard-first users and clearer ARIA labeling on timeline nodes.

2025-03-01 - Marco Li: Prepared final prototype and exported frames. Created PRD link and opened implementation spike with ENG-70123. Noted trade-offs: simplified rollback confirmation to reduce friction at expense of additional audit annotation requirement.
2025-03-02 - Ravi Shah (PM): In-review — minor copy tweaks suggested for micro-briefs and emergency modal. Approved prototype for engineering spike pending ENG validation on signal availability.
decisions: Use card-collage layout (compact cards in a horizontal timeline) to maximize scannability for non-engineer roles
Provide 1-click rollback from Emergency Rollback card with mandatory free-text annotation; skip password re-entry to speed mitigation for high-severity incidents
Surface three default observability signals (p95 latency, error rate delta, token cost delta) and allow advanced users to replace signals via Composer settings
Annotate 'Invoker role' and 'Rollback scope' on the action card to reduce operator ambiguity

ux_research_findings: Non-engineer participants preferred concise one-line briefs with a clear 'what to watch' indicator
Confusion arose when rollback scope was ambiguous — added explicit region/pool labels resolved this
One-tap rollback increased confidence only when 'Invoker role' and audit annotation were visible
